test_title: PYST 4: SSC Stenographer - English (Held on: 12 Nov 2021 Shift 2 )
subject: english
question:
**Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

The doctor asked me angrily why I had disturbed him at that late hour.

options.text: The doctor said to me, “Why I had disturbed him at that late hour?”
The doctor said to me, “Why will you have disturbed him at this late hour?”
The doctor said to me, “Why did you disturbing me at that late hour?”
The doctor said to me, “Why have you disturbed me at this late hour?”

solution:
The correct answer is: **The doctor said to me, “Why have you disturbed me at this late hour?”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is a indirect speech and we need to convert it into an direct speech..
 
• We follow these rules in Direct-Indirect speech for an interrogative sentence:
 
 
• WH – question is formed with the use of who, which, when, where, how why.
 
• A question mark should always be used at the end of an interrogative sentence in direct speech.
 
• Reported verb "**asked**" changes to "**said to**" in direct speech.
 
• The pronoun 'him' changes to 'me'.
 
• If the indirect speech is in the past perfect tense then we have to change it into present perfect tense, therefore **(had +verb +ed)** changes to **(have +verb + ed).**
 
• The pronoun 'I' changes to '**you**'.
 
• Interrogative sentence changes to assertive form [direct to indirect speech]
 
• "**that**" changes to "**this**" in direct speech.
 
 
 
• Example - 
 
 
• ​*The teacher asked me why I had not come to school the previous day. (Indirect)*
 
• *The teacher asked me, “Why did not you come to school yesterday?” (Direct)*
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

Direct sentence: *The doctor said to me, “Why have you disturbed me at this late hour?”*
